comment: E-272 (D-074, version-lifecycle.md §Components 3-4): the single list of what earlier Rein versions created and no longer do. DATA, not code — adding an entry needs no code change. class: safe = provably ours and reproducible (needs known_hashes or a rule); prompt = may hold user content (removed only with --all + confirmation); not-ours = printed, never touched. rule: not-in-src | not-in-manifest | dead-pid | stale-mtime (path predicates) | not-in-registry (kind setting) | orphan-process (kind process). Only the LAST path segment may hold a '*'.
provider_history_comment: E-270 (D-074 §Components 2): every provider name .ai/providers.json ever shipped. `ai init` drops a project provider (and any role bound to it) that is listed here but absent from the current template; a name never listed is user-added and kept.

entries.note: D-069/E-254: the gemini provider is removed. The project workspace may hold user-edited skills, so it is never removed without --all.
D-069/E-254: the agy (Antigravity) provider is removed. Same user-content risk as .gemini/.

D-069/E-254: the GEMINI.md @import shim. `ai sync` wrote it with `cp -f` from src/templates/GEMINI.md, so the sha256 of every version that file ever had in git IS the set of bytes we shipped. A GEMINI.md that hashes to none of them was edited and is reported as prompt instead.
D-069/E-254: the AGENTS.md shim for agy. Same hash evidence as GEMINI.md (src/templates/AGENTS.md had one version).
D-069/E-255: TestSprite is replaced by the headless Claude Tester. Generated tests may have been edited.

A provisioning bug created .claude/.claude/ and nothing reads it. DIVERGENCE: the blueprint's seed list implies a safe removal, but `safe` demands evidence and there is none for a whole directory tree — no manifest records it and its contents are not hash-comparable to a source path. Listed as prompt (--all + confirmation) rather than given a rule that would be true by assertion.
Pre-3.0 .ai/legacy/ holding area. May contain the operator's own notes.
E-41 backups of a third-party hook Rein replaced with a stub. They are the operator's own hooks — never removed without --all.

An agent file sync wrote for a role no longer served. Only a file recorded in _SYNC_MANIFEST.json, unmodified since, and absent from the current source set qualifies — the E-220 three-part evidence rule. Until E-273 gives .claude/agents a manifest there is no evidence and this entry matches nothing, which is the correct behaviour, not a gap.

mcp__<server>__* allow entries for a server absent from registry.json. A name that was NEVER in any shipped registry (registry_history) is the operator's own server and is kept. REPORT ONLY: `ai clean` moves paths to the trash and a JSON key is not a path — `ai init`/`ai sync` own this file (E-273). settings.local.json is user-owned and is only ever printed.

An MCP server directory in the install mirror that src/mcp/ no longer ships (e.g. intent-refiner-mcp). DIVERGENCE: the blueprint says 'not in registry', but registry.json is not the shipping list — ast-parser-mcp and shared/ are in src/mcp and in no registry, so a registry test would propose deleting live code. The mirror is a copy of src/, so src/ is the right comparand.
A hook in the mirror that hooks/ no longer ships.
A contract in the mirror that src/contracts/ no longer ships (the six v2 contracts).
The old full installer copied into HOME. It may be a version the operator keeps deliberately, so it is only listed unless --all.

An E-129 role token for a session that is over. 923 had accumulated on the operator's machine by 2026-09-17. DIVERGENCE: the blueprint says 'dead pid', but the record is keyed by Claude session id and holds {v, role, session_id, hmac} — there is no pid to test. Age is the available signal and a safe one: SessionStart re-mints a token on resume, so removing a week-old lock costs nothing.
An E-249 booted-build record whose server process is gone. A record whose pid is alive is what the staleness report reads — it is never a finding.

The worktree and throwaway HOME of an `ai ci run` that was killed: SIGKILL cannot run the cleanup trap, and one such directory held 1.3G. The directory carries no pid of its own, so the guard is the run lock: while ANY ai ci run lock has a live owner, nothing here is a finding.
The Interactive Bridge tmux watcher, removed by D-099 (E-322): SendMessage is the only Triad wake path. The installer's rsync --delete removes it; this entry covers a mirror built by the cp fallback.
The signal.json writer behind `ai handoff` and handoff_control, both removed by D-099 (E-322).
The single-writer lock of a project's ai-watch (D-099 removed the watcher). Stale once the pid it records is gone; a watcher still running from an older install keeps it.

The handoff queue ai-watch consumed (D-099: wakes go by SendMessage and are never queued). It records no pid, so the guard is the watcher lock: while a watcher from an older install still runs, nothing here is a finding.
The short-lived write lock of signal.json, left behind when a writer was killed mid-append. Same guard as the queue.

An ai-watch process whose cwd is under the temp root and which holds no project watcher lock — a test fixture that outlived its suite. 24 were alive on 2026-09-17, some over a day old. `ai start` runs a watcher from a real project, never from the temp root, and a watcher the operator is using holds .ai/.ai-watch.lock, so both halves are needed and neither is ppid: a process whose parent has exited but not been reaped still reports the zombie as its parent. Processes are signalled TERM then KILL, never trashed.
Antigravity's own user data, including OAuth credentials. NOT an Rein artefact: printed so the operator can decide, never touched by any flag.
